title: The Evening Brief: Liverpool's new owners, a coaching return, and LIV's cash crunch
dek: Tuesday's biggest news was structural: new investors at Liverpool, Mourinho back at Real Madrid, and LIV Golf cutting $30 million in prize money as its Saudi backing winds down after this season.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: The day's clearest throughline is money and leadership changing hands, at Liverpool, Real Madrid, Michigan State, and LIV Golf, while three separate injury reports filled out rosters without changing any competitive outcome yet.
bottom_line: Tuesday's news was defined by ownership and leadership changing hands, at Liverpool, Real Madrid, and Michigan State, alongside three separate injury reports for Swanson, Tyson, and Hall that filled out rosters without altering any competitive outcome yet. LIV Golf's financial strain deepened, with $30 million cut from season-ending prize money, a $60.1 million total shortfall for the year, and vendors including a $1.1 million creditor still awaiting payment as the league seeks new investment ahead of the Saudi PIF's funding ending after this season. The reporting establishes the ownership, coaching, and personnel facts plainly, while LIV's path to new funding and several injury return timelines remain open. Coming checkpoints include the BC Partners funding decision, regulatory sign-off on Liverpool's sale, Michigan State's formal hire announcement, and the Sept. 13 kickoff dates that will test whether Tyson and Hall are ready to play.
body: Tuesday's news centered on ownership, leadership, and money rather than results on the field. A consortium named 1892 Holdings, led by Amit Bhatia and including Jeff Bezos and Eduardo Saverin, acquired approximately 38% of Liverpool FC from Fenway Sports Group in a deal BBC Sport values between £5bn and £6bn, with an option to buy a controlling stake within 12 months. José Mourinho was officially unveiled as Real Madrid's manager on a three-year contract, his first time back at the club since 2013, ahead of Saturday's opener against Espanyol. Michigan State moved to finalize the hire of Dan Bartholomae, Western Michigan's athletic director since January 2022, filling the vacancy left by J Batt's departure to Kentucky.

The day's other major thread was injuries. Cubs shortstop Dansby Swanson has a Grade 2 oblique strain and is expected to miss four to six weeks, a timeline that could end his regular season as Chicago defends its wild-card position. Saints rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson could miss roughly two months after a hamstring injury in a joint practice with Jacksonville, sidelining him through at least Week 6. Jets running back Breece Hall strained his right groin in practice and is expected to miss two to three weeks, though coach Aaron Glenn said Hall is expected to be ready for the Sept. 13 opener against Tennessee.

LIV Golf's financial situation continued to deepen. The league canceled its Michigan team championship and cut the Indianapolis season-closer's purse from $20 million to $10.1 million, reducing combined payouts by $30 million; the total in lost prize money for players and teams across the 2026 season now stands at $60.1 million, per Front Office Sports. That comes as vendors report unpaid invoices ranging from thousands to nearly $100,000, with one company, Mobii Systems Group Limited, claiming it is owed more than $1.1 million. The Saudi PIF announced in April it will stop funding LIV after the 2026 season, and the league is pursuing new investment, reportedly including a possible deal with BC Partners' credit division, while it has filed a WARN Act notice and issued 30-day termination notices to some contractors.

Elsewhere, the Scottish FA said it will not back Gianni Infantino's 2027 FIFA re-election bid, joining England, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland and aligning with UEFA's 55 member associations, which have threatened a boycott of FIFA competitions; Scottish FA chief executive Ian Maxwell cited governance failures and a lack of transparency. The Premier League said it will publish full verdicts from its Key Match Incidents Panel on referee and VAR decisions for the first time this season. The AFL Tribunal upheld Jacob van Rooyen's three-match suspension, rejecting Melbourne's appeal and its biomechanist evidence, which keeps van Rooyen out for the Western Bulldogs game and the Demons' first two finals. Scottie Scheffler won the FedEx St. Jude Championship by eight shots to open the FedEx Cup Playoffs. The desk also reported the deaths of two significant figures in sports history: O.J. Brigance, the Ravens' longtime player engagement adviser and Super Bowl XXXV champion, died August 17 at 56 after a 19-year battle with ALS, and Bill Rasmussen, who founded ESPN and launched the network on Sept. 7, 1979, died at 93 from complications of Parkinson's disease.

The reporting does not explain why several of these moves landed on the same day; Liverpool's sale, Mourinho's unveiling, and Michigan State's hire appear to be independent processes reaching completion in the same window rather than connected events. LIV Golf's financial pressure is better explained: the PIF's April announcement that it will end funding after this season set a countdown that vendor non-payment, the WARN Act filing, and the prize-money cuts all point back to, though the reporting stops short of saying the league will not finish the season.
No desk boards were available this run, so today's figures come from the day's own stories rather than a separate scoreboard check.

The coming days carry several concrete checkpoints. Watch for whether BC Partners completes a funding commitment for LIV Golf and on what terms, any court filings from Mobii or other vendors, and whether the PIF's final disbursement covers outstanding invoices. Regulatory approval of Bhatia's vice-chairman role at Liverpool and any signal on exercising the 12-month option are worth tracking, as is Michigan State's official announcement of Bartholomae's hire. On the injury front, Swanson's four-to-six-week window runs into late September, Tyson's timeline is measured against the Sept. 13 opener, and Hall's return is expected in time for that same date against Tennessee. FIFA's governance committee response to the ineligibility challenge against Infantino, and whether confederations beyond UEFA's 55 associations join Scotland, England, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland, are also on the calendar.
